analysis: The BPR-max trial executed successfully but reduced pinned-host macro validation HR@10 to 0.5262, down 0.0375 from the supplied sampled-softmax reference of 0.5637 and 0.0475 from the historical binary-loss result of 0.5737. Category HR@10 was 0.545 for Movies_and_TV, 0.555 for Industrial_and_Scientific, 0.400 for Electronics, and 0.605 for CDs_and_Vinyl. Electronics had the lowest absolute score; category-level reference metrics were not supplied, so its contribution to the regression cannot be determined. This result does not support replacing sampled-softmax with this BPR-max configuration. It does not establish whether negative weighting, regularization, or optimization behavior caused the decline. Allocated GPU time was 262.42 seconds.
code_summary: One independent GRURec network and one selected checkpoint per category, with dataset routing preserved. Each network uses 96-dimensional item embeddings, input LayerNorm/dropout, a two-layer GRU, causal attention over earlier recurrent states with 32 learned relative-distance biases, a projection, and a learned gated item-embedding residual. Normalized representations use scaled cosine scoring plus a jointly learned item bias. The objective uses 64 sampled negatives with target-collision resampling: stable BPR-max ranking loss with differentiable softmax negative weights plus 0.001 weighted squared-negative-logit regularization. Training retains seed 42, AdamW, AMP, gradient clipping, and a default maximum of 200 epochs; checkpoints are selected by validation HR@10 with NDCG tie-breaking. The predictor reconstructs the same architecture and loads exactly one checkpoint for each category; no ensemble is used.
